title: Quantitative Analysis of 92 12-Week Sub-elite Marathon Training Plans
authors: Knopp M, Appelhans D, Schonfelder M, Seiler S, Wackerhage H
population: 92 published sub-elite marathon training plans, grouped by peak-week volume (high over 90 km, middle 65-90 km, low under 65 km)
findings: Mean recommended weekly volume in the last 12 weeks before the race: 108 km (high), 59 km (middle), 43 km (low) volume plans.
Full text (PMC11065819): build-up weekly increase to the peak week averaged 3 +/- 1 km or 5 +/- 3% (high), 3 +/- 1 km or 7 +/- 3% (middle) and 2 +/- 1 km or 9 +/- 4% (low volume plans).
Full text: the longest run in the plans ranged from 35.2 km (high volume) to 30.9 km (low volume).
Authors state there is no evidence for the effectiveness of the training plans investigated.
limitations: Plans are recommendations from a convenience set; no outcome data, so effectiveness and injury safety are unknown. Marathon plans only, for sub-elite runners; the relative increase is a mean over the build-up and says nothing about single-week maximum. A practice source, not an injury study.
implications: Published marathon build-ups average roughly 5-9% weekly volume increase, i.e. at or below 10%, so a 10% soft ramp matches practice; this is a convention, not evidence of safety.
Longest runs in these plans reach about 31-35 km, a practice anchor for a marathon long-run cap but not for 5K or ultra plans.

verification.notes: Re-fetched Crossref (Sports Med Open, first author Knopp, 5 authors, 2024-05-02), Europe PMC abstract (PMID 38695978) and the open-access full text PMC11065819. Confirmed in full text: 5+/-3%, 7+/-3%, 9+/-4% weekly build-up increases, 3/3/2 km, longest run 35.2 to 30.9 km, and 'no evidence for the effectiveness' in abstract. Design changed from book-or-guideline to other (quantitative analysis of published plans). Level D (practice source).
